q: New LS formed. Max strength after recent constitutional change on reserved seats?
expl: LS max 550 post-104th; Anglo-Indian reservation ended, states/UTs cap 550.
why: Post-104th cap is 530 states plus 20 UTs. Higher numbers confuse with older proposals.

q: RS composition puzzle for SI exam. Correct makeup?
expl: RS max 250: 238 elected, 12 nominated for art, science, service.
why: Nominated bring expertise. Elected bulk keeps federal balance for states.

q: Houses must meet regularly. Minimum gap rule?
options: No more than 6 months between sittings
expl: Constitution mandates House sittings with max 6-month gap.
why: Gap rule ensures executive accountability. Long prorogation without sitting violates mandate.

q: Money Bill route: Speaker role and RS time?
options: Speaker certifies; RS must return in 14 days
expl: Speaker certifies Money Bill under 109-110; RS 14 days only recommendatory.
why: Certification guards LS supremacy on finance. RS delay cannot kill money needs.

q: AP has two Houses while most states have one. Correct?
options: AP bicameral with Council plus Assembly
expl: AP is bicameral: Assembly plus Legislative Council.
why: Council is revisory second chamber. Most states are unicameral, AP retains Council.

q: Ordinary Bill stuck between Houses. Joint sitting allowed?
expl: Joint sitting under 108 only for ordinary Bills, not Money or Constitution.
why: Ordinary deadlock needs resolution mechanism. Money and amendment have separate special routes.

q: Speaker faces removal motion. Correct process?
expl: Speaker removed by LS majority after 14 days notice.
why: Notice protects neutrality. Simple House majority decides, no outside authority.

q: PAC examines public money. Strength and head?
expl: PAC 22: 15 LS 7 RS, chair from opposition by convention.
why: Opposition chair ensures credible audit of executive spending. Numbers fixed by rule.

q: State wants Council created. Route?
expl: Art 169: Assembly special majority resolution, then Parliament creates/abolishes.
why: Council birth needs state wish plus Union law. Neither alone suffices.

q: RS role on Money Bill if it withholds for 20 days?
expl: If RS misses 14 days, Money Bill deemed passed in LS form.
why: Deeming prevents financial hostage. LS will prevails after timeout.

q: Compare LS vs RS tenure. Correct?
options: LS 5 years dissolvable; RS permanent with 1/3rd retire 2 years
expl: LS term 5 years unless dissolved; RS continuing, third retires biennially.
why: Continuity gives RS stability. LS reflects fresh mandate, dissolvable earlier.

q: Compare Speaker cert vs joint sitting. Correct?
options: Speaker cert for Money bars joint sitting; ordinary allows it
expl: Money plus Constitution excluded from joint sitting; ordinary only.
why: Money has LS supremacy route. Amendment needs special majority in each House separately.

q: Compare PAC vs Estimates Committee. Correct?
options: PAC 22 opposition chair; Estimates 30 all LS
expl: PAC 22 mixed with opposition chair; Estimates 30 LS only.
why: Composition reflects audit vs estimate scrutiny. Mixing numbers is common trap.

q: Compare Council vs Assembly powers on Money. Correct?
options: Council can only delay 14 days like RS
expl: Council subordinate on Money; 14-day recommendatory role only.
why: Assembly supremacy on finance mirrors LS-RS logic. Delay cannot veto.

q: Compare privilege vs free speech in House. Correct?
options: Speech protected in House subject to rules and privilege law
expl: Speech in House protected but governed by rules, privilege, Court review limited.
why: Privilege enables debate without fear. Abuse can still face House discipline and limited review.

q: Statements: 1 LS max 550 post change. 2 RS max 250 with 12 nominated. 3 Gap max 6 months. Correct?
expl: 550 cap, 250/12 makeup, 6-month gap all settled.
why: All three state numeric constitutional design. No statement overclaims.

q: Statements: 1 Money needs Speaker cert. 2 RS can kill Money by delay. 3 Joint sitting for Money allowed. Correct?
expl: Cert true; RS only 14-day recommend; Money excluded from joint sitting.
why: Statements 2 and 3 grant RS powers it lacks. LS supremacy defeats both claims.

q: Statements: 1 Constitution amendment allows joint sitting. 2 Ordinary Bill allows it. 3 Speaker removal needs 14-day notice. Correct?
expl: Amendment excluded; ordinary allowed; Speaker 14-day notice true.
why: Statement 1 transplants ordinary route to amendment. Other two state correct procedures.

q: Statements: 1 PAC 22 opposition chair. 2 Council via Assembly plus Parliament. 3 AP unicameral. Correct?
expl: PAC and 169 route true; AP bicameral with Council, so 3 false.
why: Statement 3 denies existing AP Council. First two reflect settled committee and federal process.

q: Statements: 1 RS is permanent with biennial third retirement. 2 LS can be dissolved early. 3 Money deemed passed if RS delays. Correct?
expl: RS continuity, LS dissolvable, Money deeming all true.
why: All three capture stability plus accountability plus finance supremacy. No absolute-word flaw.
